; The federal figures for each tax year this build carries: the standard
; deduction, the limits and phase-outs the worksheets use, the credit
; amounts and the tax rate schedules. Each 2025 figure names the part of the
; published source that prints it; the sources are in sources/catalog/us.
;
; Public Law 119-21 changed several 2025 figures after Rev. Proc. 2024-40
; published them (the standard deduction, the child tax credit and the
; state and local tax limit), so those are taken from the 2025 Form 1040
; instructions, which print the figures as amended.
;
; A year without figures of its own is given 2025's. The 2026 figures, from
; Rev. Proc. 2025-32, are not yet in the source catalog.
(use-proto 'nexteggapp.taxcalcs.returns.v1 'ret)

(use-proto 'nexteggapp.taxprotos.us.federal.v1 'fed)

(use-proto 'nexteggapp.taxprotos.facts.v1 'facts)

(use-proto 'nexteggapp.taxprotos.common.v1 'common)

; Household, age attainment (January 1 rule), filing status eligibility and
; resolution (26 U.S.C. §§ 1, 2, 7703), and Section 152 dependency and Child
; Tax Credit / Other Dependent Credit tests (26 U.S.C. §§ 24, 152).
(def person-age-end-of-year ((dob Date) (tax-year Int)) Int :cite ((law "26 C.F.R." "1.152-1") (doc "us-irs-rev-rul-2003-72")) (withs (yr (date-year dob) mo (date-month dob) dy (date-day dob)) (if (<= yr 0) 0 (if (and (is mo 1) (is dy 1)) (+ (- tax-year yr) 1) (- tax-year yr)))))

(def born-before-65-cutoff? ((dob Date) (tax-year Int)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "63" "(f)(1)")) (>= (person-age-end-of-year dob tax-year) 65))

(def valid-employment-ssn? ((tin ret/TaxpayerID)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "24" "(h)(7)")) (all-of (is (. tin 'kind) 'ret/TAXPAYER_ID_KIND_SSN) (. tin 'valid_for_employment)))

(def valid-dependent-tin? ((tin ret/TaxpayerID)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "24" "(h)(4)") (law "26 U.S.C." "151" "(e)")) (any-of (is (. tin 'kind) 'ret/TAXPAYER_ID_KIND_SSN) (is (. tin 'kind) 'ret/TAXPAYER_ID_KIND_ITIN) (is (. tin 'kind) 'ret/TAXPAYER_ID_KIND_ATIN)))

(def qualifying-child-relationship? ((rel ret/Relationship)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "152" "(c)(2)")) (any-of (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_CHILD) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_STEPCHILD) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_FOSTER_CHILD) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_GRANDCHILD) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_SIBLING) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_HALF_SIBLING) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_STEPSIBLING) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_NIECE_OR_NEPHEW) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_OTHER_DESCENDANT_OF_SIBLING)))

(def qualifying-relative-relationship-or-household? ((dep ret/Dependent)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "152" "(d)(2)")) (withs (rel (. dep 'relationship)) (any-of (qualifying-child-relationship? rel) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_PARENT) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_STEPPARENT) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_GRANDPARENT) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_AUNT_OR_UNCLE) (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_IN_LAW) (all-of (is rel 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_NOT_RELATED) (is (. dep 'months_lived_with_you) 12)))))

(def passes-joint-return-test? ((dep ret/Dependent)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "152" "(b)(2)")) (any-of (not (. dep 'files_joint_return)) (. dep 'joint_return_only_for_refund)))

(def passes-citizen-test? ((dep ret/Dependent)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "152" "(b)(3)")) (. dep 'citizen_or_resident_of_north_america))

(def qualifying-child-core? ((dep ret/Dependent) (tax-year Int)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "152" "(c)")) (withs (age (person-age-end-of-year (. dep 'date_of_birth) tax-year) age-ok (any-of (< age 19) (all-of (< age 24) (. dep 'full_time_student)) (. dep 'permanently_disabled)) residency-ok (any-of (> (. dep 'months_lived_with_you) 6) (is (. dep 'custodial_release) 'ret/CUSTODIAL_RELEASE_RELEASED_TO_YOU))) (all-of (qualifying-child-relationship? (. dep 'relationship)) age-ok residency-ok (not (. dep 'provided_over_half_own_support)) (passes-joint-return-test? dep) (passes-citizen-test? dep))))

(def qualifying-child? ((dep ret/Dependent) (tax-year Int)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "152" "(c)") (law "26 U.S.C." "152" "(e)")) (all-of (qualifying-child-core? dep tax-year) (not (. dep 'not_claimed)) (not (is (. dep 'custodial_release) 'ret/CUSTODIAL_RELEASE_RELEASED_BY_YOU))))

(def ctc-qualifying-child? ((dep ret/Dependent) (tax-year Int)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "24" "(c)") (law "26 U.S.C." "24" "(h)(7)")) (all-of (qualifying-child? dep tax-year) (< (person-age-end-of-year (. dep 'date_of_birth) tax-year) 17) (valid-employment-ssn? (. dep 'tin))))

(def qualifying-relative? ((dep ret/Dependent) (tax-year Int) (p FederalYear)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "152" "(d)")) (all-of (not (qualifying-child-core? dep tax-year)) (not (. dep 'qualifying_child_of_another_taxpayer)) (qualifying-relative-relationship-or-household? dep) (< (. dep 'gross_income) (. p 'qr_gross_income_limit)) (any-of (. dep 'you_provided_over_half_support) (. dep 'multiple_support_agreement)) (passes-joint-return-test? dep) (passes-citizen-test? dep) (not (. dep 'not_claimed))))

(def odc-qualifying-dependent? ((dep ret/Dependent) (tax-year Int) (p FederalYear)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "24" "(h)(4)")) (all-of (valid-dependent-tin? (. dep 'tin)) (any-of (all-of (qualifying-child? dep tax-year) (not (ctc-qualifying-child? dep tax-year))) (qualifying-relative? dep tax-year p))))

(def claimed-dependent? ((dep ret/Dependent) (tax-year Int) (p FederalYear)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "152" "(a)")) (all-of (valid-dependent-tin? (. dep 'tin)) (any-of (qualifying-child? dep tax-year) (qualifying-relative? dep tax-year p))))

(def count-ctc-children ((deps (Slice ret/Dependent)) (tax-year Int)) Int (len (keep (fn ((d ret/Dependent)) Bool (ctc-qualifying-child? d tax-year)) deps)))

(def count-odc-dependents ((deps (Slice ret/Dependent)) (tax-year Int) (p FederalYear)) Int (len (keep (fn ((d ret/Dependent)) Bool (odc-qualifying-dependent? d tax-year p)) deps)))

(def has-hoh-qualifying-person? ((hh ret/Household) (tax-year Int) (p FederalYear)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "2" "(b)(1)")) (withs (deps (. hh 'dependents)) (any-of (some (fn ((d ret/Dependent)) Bool (all-of (> (. d 'months_lived_with_you) 6) (any-of (qualifying-child-core? d tax-year) (all-of (qualifying-relative? d tax-year p) (not (is (. d 'relationship) 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_NOT_RELATED)))))) deps) (all-of (. hh 'paid_over_half_cost_of_parents_home) (some (fn ((d ret/Dependent)) Bool (all-of (is (. d 'relationship) 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_PARENT) (qualifying-relative? d tax-year p))) deps)))))

(def eligible-for-qss? ((hh ret/Household) (tax-year Int)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "2" "(a)")) (withs (died-yr (date-year (. hh 'earlier_spouse_died_on)) deps (. hh 'dependents)) (all-of (is (. hh 'marital_status) 'ret/MARITAL_STATUS_WIDOWED) (any-of (is died-yr (- tax-year 1)) (is died-yr (- tax-year 2))) (. hh 'paid_over_half_cost_of_home) (some (fn ((d ret/Dependent)) Bool (all-of (is (. d 'months_lived_with_you) 12) (any-of (is (. d 'relationship) 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_CHILD) (is (. d 'relationship) 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_STEPCHILD)) (qualifying-child? d tax-year))) deps))))

(def considered-unmarried-for-hoh? ((hh ret/Household) (tax-year Int)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "7703" "(b)")) (all-of (is (. hh 'marital_status) 'ret/MARITAL_STATUS_MARRIED) (. hh 'spouse_absent_last_six_months) (. hh 'paid_over_half_cost_of_home) (some (fn ((d ret/Dependent)) Bool (all-of (> (. d 'months_lived_with_you) 6) (any-of (is (. d 'relationship) 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_CHILD) (is (. d 'relationship) 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_STEPCHILD) (is (. d 'relationship) 'ret/RELATIONSHIP_FOSTER_CHILD)) (qualifying-child? d tax-year))) (. hh 'dependents))))

(def resolve-filing-status ((hh ret/Household) (elections ret/Elections) (tax-year Int) (p FederalYear)) fed/FilingStatus :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "1") (law "26 U.S.C." "2") (law "26 U.S.C." "7703")) (withs (elected (. elections 'filing_status) marital (. hh 'marital_status)) (cond ((is elected 'ret/FILING_STATUS_ELECTION_SINGLE) 'fed/FILING_STATUS_SINGLE) ((is elected 'ret/FILING_STATUS_ELECTION_MARRIED_FILING_JOINTLY) 'fed/FILING_STATUS_MARRIED_FILING_JOINTLY) ((is elected 'ret/FILING_STATUS_ELECTION_MARRIED_FILING_SEPARATELY) 'fed/FILING_STATUS_MARRIED_FILING_SEPARATELY) ((is elected 'ret/FILING_STATUS_ELECTION_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD) 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD) ((is elected 'ret/FILING_STATUS_ELECTION_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE) 'fed/FILING_STATUS_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE) ((is marital 'ret/MARITAL_STATUS_MARRIED) (if (considered-unmarried-for-hoh? hh tax-year) 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD 'fed/FILING_STATUS_MARRIED_FILING_JOINTLY)) ((eligible-for-qss? hh tax-year) 'fed/FILING_STATUS_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE) ((and (. hh 'paid_over_half_cost_of_home) (has-hoh-qualifying-person? hh tax-year p)) 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD) (else 'fed/FILING_STATUS_SINGLE))))

; The name as on the Social Security card: first name, middle initial, last
; name and suffix.
(def person-full-name ((person ret/Person)) String (join-words (slice (. person 'first_name) (. person 'middle_initial) (. person 'last_name) (. person 'suffix))))

; A dependent's name: first name, last name and suffix.
(def dependent-full-name ((d ret/Dependent)) String (join-words (slice (. d 'first_name) (. d 'last_name) (. d 'suffix))))

(def lookup-dependent-by-id ((hh ret/Household) (dep-id String)) ret/Dependent (fold (fn ((acc ret/Dependent) (d ret/Dependent)) ret/Dependent (if (is (. d 'id) dep-id) d acc)) (proto 'ret/Dependent) (. hh 'dependents)))

(def build-party-for-person ((person ret/Person)) common/Party (proto 'common/Party :name (person-full-name person) :tin (. person 'tin.number)))

(def build-form1040-dependents ((deps (Slice ret/Dependent)) (tax-year Int) (p FederalYear)) (Slice fed/Dependent) (map (fn ((d ret/Dependent)) fed/Dependent (proto 'fed/Dependent :name (dependent-full-name d) :tin (. d 'tin.number) :child_tax_credit (ctc-qualifying-child? d tax-year) :credit_for_other_dependents (odc-qualifying-dependent? d tax-year p))) (keep (fn ((d ret/Dependent)) Bool (claimed-dependent? d tax-year p)) deps)))

; Form W-2 wages, Schedule B (Form 1099-INT, Form 1099-OID, Form 1099-DIV),
; Form 1099-G unemployment compensation, and the State and Local Income Tax
; Refund Worksheet (26 U.S.C. §§ 61, 85, 103, 111).
(def non-statutory-w2s ((w2s (Slice ret/W2Document))) (Slice ret/W2Document) (keep (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Bool (is (. w 'statutory_employee_business) "")) w2s))

(def w2-box12-code-sum ((w ret/W2Document) (code String)) Money (sum (fn ((ca fed/FormW2.CodedAmount)) Money (if (is (. ca 'code) code) (. ca 'amount) #usd"0.00")) (. w 'form.coded_amounts)))

(def total-w2-wages ((docs ret/Documents)) Money :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "61" "(a)(1)") (doc "us-irs-1040-instructions-2025" "line-1a")) (round-dollar (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (. w 'form.wages_tips_other_compensation)) (non-statutory-w2s (. docs 'w2s)))))

(def total-unreported-or-allocated-tips ((docs ret/Documents)) Money :cite ((doc "us-irs-1040-instructions-2025" "line-1c")) (round-dollar (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (. w 'form.allocated_tips)) (. docs 'w2s))))

(def total-nontaxable-combat-pay ((docs ret/Documents)) Money :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "112") (doc "us-irs-1040-instructions-2025" "line-1i")) (round-dollar (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (w2-box12-code-sum w "Q")) (. docs 'w2s))))

(def w2-employer-hsa-for-person ((docs ret/Documents) (person-id String)) Money :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "223" "(d)") (doc "us-irs-8889-instructions-2025" "line-9")) (round-dollar (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (if (is (. w 'person) person-id) (if (> (. w 'corrected_employer_hsa_contributions) #usd"0.00") (. w 'corrected_employer_hsa_contributions) (w2-box12-code-sum w "W")) #usd"0.00")) (. docs 'w2s))))

(def w2-wages-for-person ((docs ret/Documents) (person-id String)) Money (round-dollar (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (if (is (. w 'person) person-id) (. w 'form.wages_tips_other_compensation) #usd"0.00")) (non-statutory-w2s (. docs 'w2s)))))

(def w2-medicare-wages-for-person ((docs ret/Documents) (person-id String)) Money (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (if (is (. w 'person) person-id) (. w 'form.medicare_wages_and_tips) #usd"0.00")) (. docs 'w2s)))

(def w2-medicare-withheld-total ((docs ret/Documents)) Money (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (. w 'form.medicare_tax_withheld)) (. docs 'w2s)))

(def w2-ss-wages-for-person ((docs ret/Documents) (person-id String)) Money (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (if (is (. w 'person) person-id) (+ (. w 'form.social_security_wages) (. w 'form.social_security_tips)) #usd"0.00")) (. docs 'w2s)))

(def person-excess-ss-withheld ((docs ret/Documents) (person-id String) (p FederalYear)) Money :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "31" "(b)") (doc "us-irs-1040-instructions-2025" "excess-social-security")) (withs (person-w2s (keep (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Bool (is (. w 'person) person-id)) (. docs 'w2s)) ss-withheld (sum (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Money (. w 'form.social_security_tax_withheld)) person-w2s)) (if (<= (len person-w2s) 1) #usd"0.00" (round-dollar (clamp-zero (- ss-withheld (. p 'oasdi_max_tax)))))))

(def person-covered-by-workplace-plan? ((docs ret/Documents) (retire ret/Retirement) (person-id String)) Bool :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "219" "(g)(5)")) (withs (w2-covered (some (fn ((w ret/W2Document)) Bool (all-of (is (. w 'person) person-id) (. w 'form.retirement_plan))) (. docs 'w2s)) override-covered (some (fn ((pr ret/PersonRetirement)) Bool (all-of (is (. pr 'person) person-id) (. pr 'covered_by_workplace_plan_override))) (. retire 'persons))) (any-of w2-covered override-covered)))

; -- Schedule B: Interest and Ordinary Dividends ------------------------------
(def net-1099-int-taxable ((d ret/Form1099INTDocument)) Money (if (!= (. d 'activity) "") #usd"0.00" (clamp-zero (- (+ (. d 'form.interest_income) (. d 'form.savings_bond_and_treasury_interest)) (+ (. d 'form.bond_premium) (. d 'form.bond_premium_on_treasury_obligations) (. d 'nominee_interest) (. d 'accrued_interest_paid) (. d 'bond_premium_adjustment))))))

(def net-1099-oid-taxable ((d ret/Form1099OIDDocument)) Money (clamp-zero (- (+ (. d 'form.original_issue_discount) (. d 'form.other_periodic_interest) (. d 'form.original_issue_discount_on_treasury_obligations)) (+ (. d 'form.acquisition_premium) (. d 'form.bond_premium) (. d 'oid_adjustment) (. d 'nominee_oid)))))

(def total-tax-exempt-interest ((docs ret/Documents)) Money :cite ((law "26 U.S.C." "103") (doc "us-irs-1040-instructions-2025" "line-2a")) (round-dollar (+ (sum (fn ((d ret/Form1099INTDocument)) Money (clamp-zero (- (. d 'form.tax_exempt_interest) (. d 'form.bond_premium_on_tax_exempt_bond)))) (. docs 'interest)) (sum (fn ((d ret/Form1099OIDDocument)) Money (. d 'form.tax_exempt_oid)) (. docs 'original_issue_discount)) (sum (fn ((d ret/Form1099DIVDocument)) Money (. d 'form.exempt_interest_dividends)) (. docs 'dividends)))))

(def net-1099-div-ordinary ((d ret/Form1099DIVDocument)) Money (clamp-zero (- (. d 'form.ordinary_dividends) (. d 'nominee_dividends))))

(def net-1099-div-qualified ((d ret/Form1099DIVDocument)) Money (min (net-1099-div-ordinary d) (clamp-zero (- (. d 'form.qualified_dividends) (. d 'qualified_dividends_not_held_long_enough)))))

; Estimated tax: one answer per jurisdiction asked for, in
; ReturnOutputs.estimated. See docs/estimated-tax-design.md.
;

; the federal rules in 10_estimated_us.tlisp. Each state's rules are in its
; own directory, as returns/rules/states/<st>/NN_estimated.tlisp, and
; state-estimated-answer in returns/rules/states/00_states.tlisp dispatches
; to them. The states' rules land in steps; until a jurisdiction's do, its
; answer is ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_UNSUPPORTED, so a caller can already send
; EstimatedTaxInputs and read the answers' shape.

; EstimatedTaxInputs.jurisdictions names, or else federal and then every state
; in ReturnInputs.states.

; One jurisdiction's answer, by its rules.

; The estimated tax answers for a return's inputs: none unless
; ReturnInputs.estimated_tax is set.

; Estimated tax: the machinery every jurisdiction shares, parameterised by
; the jurisdiction's own figures. See docs/estimated-tax-design.md,
; "Shared machinery".
;
; It mirrors the Go package estimated, which the golden vectors in
; golden/testdata/estimated hold the answers of: the facts a jurisdiction's
; rules read, the options for the required annual payment, the due dates and
; their shares, crediting payments and withholding, the annualised method,
; the penalty ledger, interest by the day over a dated rate table, the
; standard waiver, what to pay next, and the text of every answer.
;
; Amounts are Money, exact. Rates and shares are Int: shares in basis points
; (25% is 2500), as money.Rate holds them, and interest rates in millionths
; (7% is 70000), as money.FineRate does, so every charge is exact rational
; arithmetic rounded once, to the cent, as the Go code rounds it.
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Text: amounts, percentages, dates and counts as a sentence writes them.
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
; The digits of n, which is not negative, with a comma every three.
(def est-group ((n Int)) String :cite () (if (< n 1000) (int-to-string n) (withs (r (- n (* (/ n 1000) 1000))) (concat (slice (est-group (/ n 1000)) "," (if (< r 10) "00" (< r 100) "0" "") (int-to-string r))))))

; An amount in whole dollars with thousands separators, halves rounded away
; from zero, as a person reads money: $1,000, or −$1,200 with a minus sign
; (U+2212). It is money.USCents.Whole.
(def est-whole ((m Money)) String :cite () (withs (cents (money-to-cents m)) (if (< cents 0) (concat (slice "−$" (est-group (/ (- 50 cents) 100)))) (concat (slice "$" (est-group (/ (+ cents 50) 100)))))))

; A rate in basis points as a percentage, trimming trailing zeros: 22%,
; 22.5%, 22.25%. It is money.Rate.String.
(def est-percent ((bp Int)) String :cite () (withs (whole (/ bp 100) frac (- bp (* whole 100))) (if (is frac 0) (concat (slice (int-to-string whole) "%")) (is (- frac (* (/ frac 10) 10)) 0) (concat (slice (int-to-string whole) "." (int-to-string (/ frac 10)) "%")) (concat (slice (int-to-string whole) "." (if (< frac 10) "0" "") (int-to-string frac) "%")))))

; A rate in basis points as an option id writes it: 90, or 66.67.
(def est-id-percent ((bp Int)) String :cite () (withs (whole (/ bp 100) frac (- bp (* whole 100))) (if (is frac 0) (int-to-string whole) (concat (slice (int-to-string whole) "." (if (< frac 10) "0" "") (int-to-string frac))))))

(= est-month-names (Slice String) (slice "January" "February" "March" "April" "May" "June" "July" "August" "September" "October" "November" "December"))

; A date as a form prints it: April 15, 2026.
(def est-long-date ((d Date)) String :cite () (concat (slice (elt est-month-names (- (date-month d) 1)) " " (int-to-string (date-day d)) ", " (int-to-string (date-year d)))))

; A date as Go's estimated.Date prints it in an error: 2026-03-31.
(def est-iso-date ((d Date)) String :cite () (withs (two (fn ((n Int)) String (concat (slice (if (< n 10) "0" "") (int-to-string n))))) (concat (slice (int-to-string (date-year d)) "-" (two (date-month d)) "-" (two (date-day d))))))

(= est-short-month-names (Slice String) (slice "Jan" "Feb" "Mar" "Apr" "May" "Jun" "Jul" "Aug" "Sep" "Oct" "Nov" "Dec"))

; A date as a summary writes it: Dec 31, 2026.
(def est-short-date ((d Date)) String :cite () (concat (slice (elt est-short-month-names (- (date-month d) 1)) " " (int-to-string (date-day d)) ", " (int-to-string (date-year d)))))

(= est-count-words (Slice String) (slice "no" "one" "two" "three" "four" "five" "six" "seven" "eight" "nine"))

; A count in words below ten, and in digits from ten.
(def est-count ((n Int)) String :cite () (if (and (>= n 0) (< n 10)) (elt est-count-words n) (int-to-string n)))

; What is left after a subtraction, for a sentence: "leaves $742", or "leaves
; a $136 refund" below zero. A refund is never written with a minus sign.
(def est-leaves ((left Money)) String :cite () (if (< left #usd"0.00") (concat (slice "leaves a " (est-whole (- #usd"0.00" left)) " refund")) (concat (slice "leaves " (est-whole left)))))

; est-leaves in the past tense, for last year.
(def est-left ((left Money)) String :cite () (if (< left #usd"0.00") (concat (slice "left a " (est-whole (- #usd"0.00" left)) " refund")) (concat (slice "left " (est-whole left)))))

; The effect of asking for this year's tax: while another option sets the

(def est-rate-of ((bp Int) (m Money)) Money :cite () (round-cents (/ (* m bp) 10000)))

; taxed at rate_bp basis points. The top band's ceiling is a sentinel far
; above any income.

; The tax on taxable income through a rate schedule, each band figured on its
; own and rounded to the cent, as the rate schedules print it. A state that
; rounds each band to a whole dollar, as Oregon does, says so.

; The rate is held in basis points and applied as (income * bp) / 10000, so
; the arithmetic is exact: a decimal rate such as 0.093 has no exact Float.

; How Alabama's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= al-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Alabama uses the federal estimated tax rules, with a $500 threshold, not $1,000. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall." (slice "Withholding and estimated payments avoid the penalty if they reach a target. The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. The second is 110% if last year's Alabama AGI was over $150,000. The AGI limit is $75,000 for married filing separately. Last year's figure is open only if you filed a return for a full twelve months. There is no penalty if this year's tax less withholding is under $500." "Pay a quarter each by April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. A date on a Saturday, Sunday or State holiday shifts to the next business day. Withholding counts as paid evenly on the four dates. You can instead show when it was actually withheld. The department sends no record of your payments, so keep your own." "The penalty is interest on each shortfall for the days it stays unpaid. The department's rate follows the federal underpayment rate each quarter. Interest stops on April 15 of the next year. A payment goes first to the oldest shortfall. The 2025 penalty form prints 7% for the whole year. For 2026 the rate is 6% from April to June and 7% after. If income came unevenly, Schedule AI's annualised method can cut early payments. The department can waive the penalty for a casualty or disaster. It can also do so for retirement after 62 or disability, with reasonable cause." "By adopting the federal rules, the statute grants two things the forms omit. The January payment has no penalty if you file and pay in full by January 31. There is no penalty after a full year with no Alabama tax liability. The department's forms apply neither. If you first need to pay after April 1, Form 40ES says a third by June 15. After June 1 it says half by September 15. The penalty form still charges a quarter by every date.") "Alabama's threshold is $500 rather than $1,000, the federal figure. The 110% test reads last year's Alabama AGI. Alabama's State holidays move a due date. The forms charge the January payment even if you file and pay by January 31. They also charge someone who had no tax last year. The statute excuses both." (slice "Code of Ala. §§ 40-18-80, 40-1-44 and 1-3-8; 26 U.S.C. § 6654" "Form 40ES and its instructions, 2026" "Form 2210AL and its instructions, 2025" "Alabama Department of Revenue, Quarterly Interest Rates")))

; residents.
;
; Arkansas does not start from federal adjusted gross income: it lists each
; kind of income as Arkansas counts it, taken here from the prepared federal
; return. Social security, military pay and military retirement are left out,
; and the first $6,000 of pension and IRA income is excluded.
;
; Only column A is modelled, so filing status 4 (married filing separately on
; the same return) is not. The rules take the standard deduction and the
; regular tax table; the low income tables and itemized deductions are not
; modelled.

; the form and instructions they implement name them in
; sources/catalog/ar/2025.

; row whose floor is the largest not above the income, and above the table
; $3,809 plus 3.9% of the excess over $100,000.

"26-51-201")) (withs (ti (clamp-zero income)) (if (> ti (. y 'table_ceiling)) (+ (. y 'table_ceiling_tax) (round-dollar (/ (* (- ti (. y 'table_ceiling)) (int-to-float (. y 'top_rate_bp))) 10000.0))) (fold (fn ((acc Money) (row ArkansasTaxRow)) Money (if (<= (. row 'floor) ti) (. row 'tax) acc)) #usd"0.00" ar-regular-table-2025))))

; Arkansas's estimated tax under the Income Tax Act of 1987, worked through on
; Form AR2210, or on Form AR2210A for the annualized method. It is written on
; the shared machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and
; reproduces the Go rules in arkansastaxcalc/estimated.go, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/AR.json.gz holds.
;
; The figures follow the Department of Finance and Administration's forms:
; the 2026 AR1000ES, and the 2025 AR2210, its instructions and AR2210A, the
; latest published. AR2210 is not Form 2210: withholding and the estimated
; payments made by the last due date count as paid in four equal parts on the
; due dates, whenever they were made; the penalty is a fixed 10% a year over
; 365 days, each charge in whole dollars; and a return filed and paid by
; January 31 removes the year's penalty. The Arkansas Code's text was not
; retrieved, so the statutory side of each divergence is the instructions'
; restatement of the law. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the 2026 AR1000ES prints them.
(defstruct ArkansasEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (this_year_rate Int) (penalty_rate Int) (due_dates (Slice Date)))

(deffigures ar-estimated-2026 ArkansasEstimatedYear 2026 (from ar-dfa-form-ar1000es-2026 (this_year_rate 9000 :at underestimate-of-tax) (penalty_rate 1000 :at underestimate-of-tax) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at vouchers)))

; AR2210A give it.

; How Arkansas's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= ar-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Arkansas expects estimated payments if your tax after withholding tops $1,000. The penalty is a flat 10% a year on each quarter's shortfall while it's unpaid." (slice "You avoid the penalty if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. It is the smaller of 90% of this year's Arkansas tax and 100% of last year's. There is no 110% tier, so last year's tax works at any income. There's no penalty if tax less Arkansas withholding is $1,000 or less this year. There is also none if you had no Arkansas tax liability last year. That year must be a full year in which you lived in Arkansas throughout." "A quarter is due April 15, June 15 and September 15, and January 15 next year. The department's penalty form spreads withholding evenly across the four dates. It does the same with estimated payments made by January 15. Both count that way whenever they were actually made. So paying late in the year still counts toward the earlier dates. Filing your return and paying the tax by January 31 removes the year's penalty." "The penalty works like interest at a fixed 10% a year. Each shortfall is charged for each day from its due date until it's paid. The charge stops at April 15 of the next year if that comes first. A payment goes to the oldest shortfall first. If your income came unevenly, Form AR2210A can lower the early installments. The Commissioner can excuse the penalty for a casualty or disaster. The Commissioner can also excuse it if you retired after 62 or became disabled. That needs reasonable cause." "The department's own documents disagree on a few details. One is whether exactly $1,000 is inside the rules. Another is whether an estimated payment counts from the day it's made.") "Arkansas differs from federal in five ways that can change a number. The penalty is a fixed 10% a year rather than the quarterly federal rate. There's no 110% tier. Estimated payments count as made evenly through the year. Filing and paying by January 31 removes the penalty for the whole year. The no-liability exception needs Arkansas residence all of last year." (slice "AR1000ES, Estimated Tax Declaration Vouchers and Instructions for Tax Year 2026" "AR2210, Penalty for Underpayment of Estimated Tax, and its instructions, 2025" "AR2210A, Annualized Penalty for Underpayment of Estimated Income Tax, 2025" "DFA Subject 603, Penalty for Underpayment of Estimated Tax (rev. 12/22/2020)")))

; The 2026 rules. The 2026 AR2210 and AR2210A are not published, so their
; figures are the 2025 forms' with the 2026 dates: the $1,000 threshold, the
; 100% test, the four equal parts, the April 15 stop, the 365-day year, the
; January 31 date of Exception 2, and AR2210A's periods, percentages and
; daily factor. A figure's source must be for its year, so these are written
; out rather than deffigures. No holiday is listed: the four 2026 due dates
; are weekdays.
(= ar-estimated-rules-2026 ArkansasEstimatedRules (make-struct ArkansasEstimatedRules :figures ar-estimated-2026 :threshold #usd"1000.00" :last_year_rate 10000 :shares (slice 2500 2500 2500 2500) :file_and_pay_by #date"2027-01-31" :stop #date"2027-04-15" :year_days 365 :rate_source "AR1000ES (2026), Underestimate of Tax: ten percent (10%) per annum" :period_ends (slice #date"2026-03-31" #date"2026-05-31" #date"2026-08-31" #date"2026-12-31") :annualised_shares (slice 2250 4500 6750 9000) :factor 27397 :factor_source "AR2210A (2025), line 43: .00027397 a day" :explanation ar-estimated-explanation))

; Arizona's estimated tax: A.R.S. § 43-581, with the penalty of
; § 42-1125(Q) and the interest of § 42-1123, worked through on Form 221,
; Arizona's own underpayment form. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; arizonataxcalc/estimated.go, whose answers golden/testdata/estimated/AZ.json.gz
; holds.
;
; § 43-581(D) asks the department for rules "similar to" the Internal Revenue
; Code, and the forms follow 26 U.S.C. § 6654 closely: four equal
; instalments on the federal dates, withholding deemed paid evenly, and the
; same annualised method. Form 221 departs from Form 2210 in three ways, which
; is why it is a form of its own: whether payments are due at all is an income
; test in both years (§ 43-581(A)); the penalty is capped at 10% of each
; underpayment (§ 42-1125(Q); line 29); and penalty unpaid on January 1 joins
; the principal it is charged on (§ 42-1123(B); line 27).

; The figures follow the 2026 Form 140ES and the 2025 Form 221, the latest
; penalty form; the answer's divergences say where the statutes read
; otherwise. Two federal facts free the filer of Arizona's penalty under
; § 43-581(E)(1): no federal tax liability last year, and federal tax less
; federal withholding under $1,000. They are read from the federal facts in the
; same request, as Colorado's rules read the federal annualising election. A
; year with no figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the 2026 Form 140ES instructions and the
; department's interest rates page print them.

; How Arizona's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these rules
; carry.
(= az-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Arizona asks for estimated payments only above a gross income threshold. Your Arizona gross income must be over $75,000 both last year and this year. On a joint return the threshold is $150,000. The penalty is interest on each quarter's shortfall. It can never be more than 10% of the shortfall." (slice "Your Arizona gross income may be at or under the threshold in either year. Then Arizona doesn't expect estimated payments and charges no penalty. That holds however much tax is due. There's also no penalty for a small balance. That's Arizona tax after credits, less Arizona withholding, under $1,000." "If you do have to pay, withholding and estimated payments must reach a target. The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. There is no 110% rule for higher incomes. The department's 2026 instructions limit last year's figure. You must have been required to file a 2025 Arizona return, and filed it. Federal relief carries over. With no federal tax liability last year, there's no Arizona penalty either. Federal tax less federal withholding under $1,000 this year does the same." "The payments are a quarter each. They're due April 15, June 15 and September 15, 2026, and January 15, 2027. A date on a weekend or legal holiday shifts to the next business day. Withholding counts as paid evenly on those dates. You can instead show when it was actually taken. You can file your 2026 return and pay in full by February 1, 2027. That replaces the January payment." "The penalty is figured like interest. The rate is the federal short-term rate plus three points. That's 6% for April to June 2026 and 7% from July. Each shortfall is charged by the day until paid. The department's form stops counting on April 15 of the next year. Penalty still unpaid on January 1 is added to the amount it's charged on. Form 221's annualised worksheet can lower early payments for uneven income. The department can waive the penalty for a casualty or disaster. Retiring after 62 or becoming disabled also counts, with reasonable cause.") "Arizona differs from federal where a number can change. Whether you must pay turns on Arizona gross income in both years. The line is over $75,000, or $150,000 joint. There's no 110% tier. The penalty can never exceed 10% of the shortfall. Penalty unpaid on January 1 is itself charged. A federal exception removes the Arizona penalty too." (slice "A.R.S. §§ 43-581, 42-1123, 42-1125(Q)" "Arizona Form 140ES and its instructions, 2026" "Arizona Form 221, Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, and its instructions, 2025" "ADOR, Interest Rates")))

; counted in the same shares; the threshold is $500; there is no prior-year

; Worksheet I; and the rate is set half-yearly. Where the Franchise Tax
; Board's forms and the statute disagree, the figure follows the form and the
; answer's divergences say what the statute says. A year with no figures is
; answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.

; How California's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= ca-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "California follows the federal idea of paying tax through the year. Payments are front-loaded: 70% of the year's requirement is due by mid-June. No penalty applies unless at least $500 is due after withholding." (slice "Withholding and estimated payments must reach a target to avoid the penalty. The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. As federally, last year's figure needs a full-year return. It becomes 110% if last year's California AGI was over $150,000. That's $75,000 if married filing separately. Unlike federal, it's unavailable once this year's California AGI is $1,000,000. That's $500,000 if married filing separately. Then only 90% of this year's tax will do." "The payments are not equal quarters. The split is 30% April 15, 40% June 15, none September 15 and 30% January 15. Withholding counts as paid in the same proportions on those dates. That holds whenever it was actually taken. A date on a weekend or holiday shifts to the next business day. Filing and paying in full by January 31 replaces the January payment." "There's no penalty if this year's tax less withholding is under $500. That's $250 if married filing separately. There's also none if last year's tax was under that. No liability on a full-year California return last year also means no penalty." "The penalty is interest on each shortfall for the days it stays unpaid. The Franchise Tax Board sets the rate each half-year from the federal rate. It stops on April 15 of the next year. The annualised method on FTB 5805 can lower early payments for uneven income. It uses 27%, 63%, 63% and 90% of annualised tax. The FTB can waive the penalty for a casualty or disaster. It can also waive it for retiring after 62 or disability, with reasonable cause. There's none to the extent a law passed during the year caused the underpayment.") "California's payments are 30%, 40%, 0% and 30%, not four equal quarters. So 70% is due by June. The threshold is $500, not $1,000. Either year's balance under it excuses the penalty. Last year's test isn't available at $1,000,000 of California AGI. The annualised percentages are 27%, 63%, 63% and 90%. The rate is set half-yearly." (slice "Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §§ 19136, 19136.1, 19136.3, 19136.7, 19521" "2026 Instructions for Form 540-ES" "FTB 5805 (2025) and its instructions" "FTB, Interest and estimate penalty rates (updated 06/22/2026)")))

(slice "You avoid the penalty if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the smaller of 70% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's. Above $150,000 of federal adjusted gross income last year, the 100% is 110%. The limit is $75,000 if you are married filing separately. Last year's figure needs a Colorado return for a full twelve-month year." "Pay a quarter by April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. A date on a weekend or legal holiday shifts to the next business day. Withholding counts as paid evenly across the four dates. You can instead show when it was actually withheld. An overpayment carried forward from last year counts toward April. Filing and paying in full by January 31 removes the January payment's penalty." "The penalty form looks at this year's tax less withholding. It charges nothing when that is $1,000 or less. The statute says less than $1,000, so the two differ only at exactly $1,000. The statute also excuses you if you had no Colorado tax liability last year. You must have lived in Colorado all of that year. The department can also waive the penalty for good cause. It can waive it too if you retired after 62 or became disabled. None of those three is on the form, DR 0204, so you have to ask for them." "The penalty is interest at Colorado's regular rate, set once each calendar year. That is 11% for 2026 and 10% for 2027. It runs by the day from each due date until the shortfall is paid. It stops on April 15 of the next year at the latest. A shortfall carried past December 31 changes rate on January 1. The lower discounted rate Colorado gives on other late tax doesn't apply. If you annualise uneven income federally, you can annualise for Colorado too. DR 0204 Part 4 uses 17.5%, 35%, 52.5% and 70% of the tax on annualised income.") "Colorado differs from federal where a number can change. The current-year test is 70%, not 90%. Last year's figure needs a filed Colorado return. The rate is Colorado's own, set once a year rather than every quarter. It is 11% for 2026 and 10% for 2027. You can annualise only if you annualise federally. ;
; The return starts from the prepared federal return: federal AGI and the
; federal filing status. Schedule 1's additions and subtractions and the
; credits come in as ConnecticutInputs; the Tax Calculation Schedule reads its
; tables from the figures in 01_params.tlisp.
;
; The rules cite the law (Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 229) and the instructions.
; The parts of the form they implement name them in sources/catalog/ct/2025.
; The Tax Calculation Schedule in the Form CT-1040 instructions, which gives
; line 6. Every line is in whole dollars: Table B's examples round the tax on
; the excess to the dollar ($2,500 x .045 = $112.50, entered as $113), and
; line 9 is the product of line 7 and a decimal, entered as dollars.
;
; The personal exemption (Table A) comes off Connecticut AGI; Table B taxes
; the rest; the 2% phase-out add-back (Table C) and the tax recapture (Table
; D) are added to it; and the personal tax credit (Table E) takes its decimal
; share of that total off. Tables A, C, D and E are all read at Connecticut
; AGI, line 1, not at taxable income.

; Connecticut's estimated tax: Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 12-701(a)(12) and 12-722,
; worked through on Form CT-2210, Connecticut's own underpayment form. It is
; written on the shared machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp
; and reproduces the Go rules in connecticuttaxcalc/estimated.go, whose
; answers golden/testdata/estimated/CT.json.gz holds.
;
; The arithmetic is federal in shape: 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last
; year's, four equal quarters, nothing under $1,000, the annualised method at
; 22.5%, 45%, 67.5% and 90%. Connecticut reenacts those rules in its own
; statute rather than adopting 26 U.S.C. § 6654. What differs, and makes
; CT-2210 a form of its own, is the charge: interest of 1% for each month or
; part of a month an underpayment stays unpaid, a month running from the 16th
; to the 15th (§ 12-722(a); Schedule B), on running totals of what was due
; and paid; and the Pass-Through Entity Tax Credit counts like withholding, on
; lines of its own.
;

; rules carry.

The tax is counted after withholding and any Pass-Through Entity Tax Credit. Paying too little by a due date costs interest of 1% a month on the shortfall." (slice "There is no interest if your payments together reach the smaller of two figures. One is 90% of this year's Connecticut tax. The other is 100% of the tax on last year's Connecticut return. Withholding and the Pass-Through Entity Tax Credit count as payments. Last year's figure needs a return that covered twelve months. Unlike the federal rules, there is no 110% figure at higher incomes." "Pay a quarter by each of Apr 15, Jun 15, Sep 15 and Jan 15 of the next year. A date on a weekend or legal holiday becomes the next business day. Withholding counts as paid evenly across the four dates. You can instead show the dates it was actually withheld. The Pass-Through Entity Tax Credit is always spread evenly. Filing and paying in full by January 31 clears interest on the January payment." "Withholding and the credit are taken off this year's tax. There is no interest if under $1,000 is left. Nor is there any if you lived in Connecticut all last year and had no tax there." "Connecticut calls the charge interest rather than a penalty. It is 1% for each month or part of a month that a shortfall stays unpaid. Months run from the 16th to the 15th, so a day late is charged a whole month. The rate is fixed by law and doesn't follow market rates. It stops when the shortfall is paid, and no later than April 15 of next year. With uneven income, Form CT-2210's annualised method can lower early payments. Connecticut's rules have no waiver for a casualty or disaster. Nor do they have one for retirement or disability.") "Connecticut charges 1% for each month or part of one, about 12% a year. Federal interest is a quarterly rate counted by the day. There is no 110% figure at higher income. ; each $50 row is taxed at its midpoint through the rate schedule and rounded
; to the dollar. In the 8.5% band, from $60,000, the printed table runs one
; dollar below that figure on every row (60,000-60,049 is $3,501, 99,950-99,999
; is $6,897), and the filer must use the table, so the rule does too. Above

; The District of Columbia's estimated tax: D.C. Code § 47-4203 and
; § 47-1812.08(i), with interest at the § 47-4201(d) rate, worked through on
; Form D-2210. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; districtofcolumbiataxcalc/estimated.go, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/DC.json.gz holds.
;
; The District's section is written on the federal pattern, but it is the
; District's own text. The prior-year test is always 110%; the threshold is
; $100; and the charge is interest at a fixed 10%, which D-2210 turns into one
; printed factor for each span between due dates, charged on each period's
; running underpayment. The figures follow the Office of Tax and Revenue's
; forms, D-40ES for 2026 and D-2210 for 2025, and the answer's divergences say
; where the D.C. Code reads otherwise. A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as D-40ES for 2026 prints them.
(defstruct DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (due_dates (Slice Date)))

(deffigures dc-estimated-2026 DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedYear 2026 (from dc-otr-form-d40es-2026 (threshold #usd"100.00" :at who-must-file) (this_year_rate 9000 :at who-must-file) (last_year_rate 11000 :at who-must-file) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-15" #date"2026-06-15" #date"2026-09-15" #date"2027-01-15") :at when-due)))

; A tax year's rules: its figures, and what D-2210 and the D.C. Code give it.
(defstruct DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedRules (figures DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedYear) (remaining Int) (shares (Slice Int)) (later_groups (Slice Date)) (stop Date) (factors (Slice Int)) (period_ends (Slice Date)) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

; How the District's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years
; these rules carry.
(= dc-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Take your DC tax due after withholding and credits. If it is $100 or more, the District expects estimated payments. The charge for paying too little or too late is called underpayment interest. Form D-2210 figures it with a printed factor for each period." (slice "There is no interest if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. The target is the smaller of 90% of this year's DC tax or 110% of last year's. The District has no 100% tier: last year's figure is 110% at every income. The form lets you use it only if you filed a DC return for last year. Otherwise only the 90% figure counts." "Pay a quarter each by April 15, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. A date on a weekend or legal holiday becomes the next business day. Withholding counts as paid evenly on the four dates. You can instead show when all of it was actually withheld. An overpayment carried from last year counts toward April. File your return and pay the balance by January 15 to skip the January payment. Interest on any earlier shortfall still runs." "D-2210 takes the amount still short at each due date. That counts everything required and paid so far. It is multiplied by a factor for the span to the next due date. The factors are .0175, .0265, .0351 and .0259, the last running to April 15. A payment made between due dates counts only from the next due date. The factors appear to spread the law's rate over each span's days. That rate is 10% a year compounded daily, about 10.5% a year. The law charges the actual days until payment, rounded up to the month's end. Its figure can therefore differ from the form's." "No interest is due if tax less withholding and estimated payments is under $100. None is due either if you had no DC tax last year and lived in DC all of it. The form also excuses a balance under 10% of the year's tax. The law doesn't mention that. The law excuses a casualty or disaster. So is someone who retired after 62 or became disabled, with reasonable cause. None of these is on D-2210, so you have to ask the Office of Tax and Revenue.") "The threshold is $100, not $1,000. Last year's figure is always 110%, with no income test. The charge is a fixed 10% compounded daily. The form excuses a balance under 10% of the year's tax. Its annualised method is a proration by income. Filing and paying by January 15, not January 31, replaces the last payment." (slice "D.C. Code §§ 47-4201(d), 47-4203, 47-1812.08(i)" "D-40ES, Estimated Payment for Individual Income Tax, 2026 (REV. 03/2026)" "D-2210, Underpayment of Estimated Income Tax By Individuals, 2025 (revised 05/2025)" "2025 D-40 booklet")))

; The 2026 rules. No 2026 D-2210 is published, so its figures are the 2025
; form's: the 10% exception, the four quarters and the four factors, which
; are the District's fixed 10% for spans of 61, 92, 122 and 90 days, the same
; lengths in 2026. The later declaration dates, the April 15 stop and the
; annualisation periods are the D.C. Code's. A figure's source must be for
; its year, so these are written out rather than deffigures. No holiday is
; listed: the four 2026 due dates are weekdays.
(= dc-estimated-rules-2026 DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedRules (make-struct DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedRules :figures dc-estimated-2026 :remaining 1000 :shares (slice 2500 2500 2500 2500) :later_groups (slice #date"2026-04-02" #date"2026-06-02" #date"2026-09-02") :stop #date"2027-04-15" :factors (slice 175 265 351 259) :period_ends (slice #date"2026-03-31" #date"2026-05-31" #date"2026-08-31" #date"2026-12-31") :explanation dc-estimated-explanation))

(= dc-estimated-years (Table Int DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedRules) (table 2026 dc-estimated-rules-2026))

; "Jun 15" in the tax year, and "Jan 15, 2027" outside it.
(def dc-short-date ((d Date) (year Int)) String :cite () (if (is (date-year d) year) (concat (slice (elt est-short-month-names (- (date-month d) 1)) " " (int-to-string (date-day d)))) (est-short-date d)))

; D-2210's 10% exception: what is left to pay is less than the share of the
; tax.
(def dc-under-remaining ((r DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedRules) (tax Money) (left Money)) Bool :cite () (< (* (max #usd"0.00" left) 10000) (* tax (. r 'remaining))))

; The share of the tax, rounded up to the cent, so that an amount is under
; it exactly when dc-under-remaining holds.
(def dc-remaining-limit ((r DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedRules) (tax Money)) Money :cite () (withs (n (* (money-to-cents (max #usd"0.00" tax)) (. r 'remaining))) (* #usd"0.01" (/ (+ n 9999) 10000))))

(def dc-remaining-question ((r DistrictOfColumbiaEstimatedRules)) ret/EstimatedQuestion :cite () (est-ask "unsettled rule" "" (concat (slice "The form excuses a balance less than " (est-percent (. r 'remaining)) " of the year's tax. The law doesn't include that exception, and the figures follow the form."))))

; Delaware's statute is short. § 1169 requires a declaration when the

; How Delaware's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= de-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Delaware expects estimated payments when your tax will be more than $800. This is your Delaware tax after withholding and credits. The penalty is 1.5% a month on each late installment. The Division's form charges it as 0.05% a day." (slice "To avoid the penalty, withholding and estimated payments must reach a target. The target is the smaller of two figures. They are 90% of this year's Delaware tax and 100% of last year's. The 100% is 110% if last year's adjusted gross income (AGI) was over $150,000. That line is $75,000 if you file separately on separate forms (filing status 3). The penalty form tests Delaware AGI. The estimated tax instructions say federal AGI. If the two fall on different sides of the line, settle it with the Division. No penalty is due if the target less your Delaware withholding is $800 or less. There is also none if you had no Delaware tax liability last year." "A quarter is due by April 30, June 15, September 15 and the next January 15. The first is April 30, not April 15, because Delaware's return is due April 30. A date on a weekend or Delaware holiday becomes the next business day. Withholding counts in the period it was taken out, not evenly across the year. Withholding from January to March counts toward April 30. April and May withholding counts toward June 15, and so on. If your income came unevenly, Form PIT-UND has an annualised method. It uses 22.5%, 45%, 67.5% and 90% of the tax on annualised income." "The law sets the penalty at 1.5% a month, or part of a month. The rate doesn't change with interest rates. The form charges by the day instead, 0.05% for each day an installment is late. Thirty days come to 1.5%. It runs from the due date, or May 1 for the first installment. It stops when the shortfall is paid, or on April 30 of the next year. The form's Short Method lets you pay 12% of the total shortfall instead. It is open if you made no estimated payments, or four equal ones on time." "The Division can waive the penalty in two cases. One is a casualty, disaster or other unusual circumstance. The other is that you retired after 62 or became disabled this year or last. You don't claim either on the form. You wait for the penalty to be assessed, then write to the Tax Conferee.") "Delaware's line is $800 of required payment less withholding, not $1,000 of tax. The penalty is a fixed 1.5% a month, not a rate set each quarter. It is charged at 0.05% a day, about 18% a year. Withholding counts when it was taken out, and there is a 12% Short Method. Federal Form 2210 is not accepted in place of PIT-UND." (slice "30 Del. ; Georgia's estimated tax: O.C.G.A. §§ 48-7-114 to 48-7-120, worked through on
; Form 500 UET, Georgia's own underpayment form. It is written on the shared
; machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the
; Go rules in georgiataxcalc/estimated.go, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/GA.json.gz holds.
;
; Georgia differs from the federal rules in shape, which is why Form 500 UET
; is a form of its own. Whether payments are required turns on gross income,
; not on tax. The current-year test is 70% of this year's tax, and the
; prior-year test is 100% of last year's at every income. Each payment goes
; first to the instalment of its own period, and only what is left over pays
; an earlier shortfall (lines 9 to 12). Three exceptions excuse an instalment
; when the payments to its date reach them (lines 13 to 16). The penalty is a
; fixed 9% a year, by the day (line 20).
;
; The statute is published officially only through LexisNexis and could not
; be read. Every rule here comes from the Department of Revenue's Form 500 UET
; (Rev. 07/15/25) and Form 500-ES (Rev. 05/12/25), and the 2026 figures from
; HB 463 (2026). A year with no figures is answered
; ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures: Form 500 UET's, which is for tax years 2025 and
; later; Form 500-ES's, the voucher the Department lists for 2026; and HB
; 463's, which changed the 2026 deductions and rate after Form 500-ES was
; printed.

; How Georgia's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these
; rules carry.
(= ga-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Georgia expects estimated payments on income that tax isn't withheld from. It charges 9% a year on each installment you underpay. Its safe harbours are lower than federal. They are 70% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's." (slice "Whether you have to pay at all turns on income, not on tax. Estimated tax is required when expected gross income exceeds three amounts. They are your dependent exemptions, your deductions and $1,000, added together. For 2026, each exemption is $5,000 and the standard deduction is $15,000. A joint return's standard deduction is $30,000. Payments aren't needed if your employer agrees to withhold enough extra." "You avoid the penalty if withholding and payments reach a target. The target is 70% of this year's Georgia tax or, if lower, 100% of last year's. Last year's counts only from a return covering twelve months. There is no 110% tier for higher incomes. The amount is paid in equal installments on April 15, June 15 and September 15. The last is due January 15 of the next year. Becoming required later in the year means fewer, larger installments. Withholding counts as paid equally each quarter, whenever it was taken. If you file and pay the balance by January 31, it counts as paid on January 15." "Each payment counts first toward its own period's installment. Only what is left over makes up an earlier shortfall. Three tests can also excuse an installment, based on what you paid by its date. One is last year's income taxed at this year's 4.99% rate. Another is 70% of the tax on your annualised income. The third, except in January, is 90% of the tax on income actually received." "The penalty is 9% a year on each shortfall, by the day from its due date. It runs until the shortfall is paid or April 15 of the next year. The rate is fixed rather than tied to the federal rate. Georgia's forms have no waiver for a casualty, retirement or disability. The Department does postpone deadlines for declared disasters.") "Georgia's test is gross income over exemptions, deductions and $1,000. It is not $1,000 of tax. The tests are 70% of this year's tax and 100% of last year's, with no 110% tier. A payment goes first to its own period's installment. Three exceptions can excuse an installment. The penalty is a fixed 9% a year. There is no casualty, retirement or disability waiver." ; instructions they implement name them in sources/catalog/hi/2025.
; The rate schedule for a filing status: Schedule I for single and separate
; filers, II for joint filers and surviving spouses, III for heads of household.
(def hi-rate-schedule ((status fed/FilingStatus)) (Slice HawaiiRateRow) :cite ((law "HRS" "235-51")) (cond ((is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_MARRIED_FILING_JOINTLY) hi-schedule-ii-2025) ((is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE) hi-schedule-ii-2025) ((is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD) hi-schedule-iii-2025) (else hi-schedule-i-2025)))

; The tax a rate schedule sets on an income: the base of the highest row the
; income is over, plus that row's rate on the excess, to the nearest dollar.
(def hi-schedule-tax ((rows (Slice HawaiiRateRow)) (income Money)) Money :cite ((law "HRS" "235-51")) (round-dollar (fold (fn ((acc Money) (row HawaiiRateRow)) Money (if (> income (. row 'floor)) (+ (. row 'base) (/ (* (- income (. row 'floor)) (int-to-float (. row 'rate_bp))) 10000.0)) acc)) #usd"0.00" rows)))

; The rate, in basis points, on the next dollar of taxable income.
(def hi-marginal-rate-bp ((rows (Slice HawaiiRateRow)) (income Money)) Int :cite ((law "HRS" "235-51")) (fold (fn ((acc Int) (row HawaiiRateRow)) Int (if (or (> income (. row 'floor)) (is (. row 'floor) #usd"0.00")) (. row 'rate_bp) acc)) 0 rows))

; Form N-11 line 27: the tax on taxable income. Below $100,000 it comes from
; the tax table, whose rows are $50 wide and whose tax is the schedule's tax
; at each row's midpoint; from $100,000 the rate schedules apply directly.
(def hi-tax ((y HawaiiYear) (status fed/FilingStatus) (taxable Money)) Money :cite ((law "HRS" "235-51") (doc "hi-dotax-form-n-11-instructions-2025" "tax-table")) (withs (ti (clamp-zero taxable) rows (hi-rate-schedule status) width (. y 'tax_table_row_width)) (if (< ti (. y 'tax_table_ceiling)) (withs (steps (floor-float (/ ti width)) midpoint (+ (* width steps) (/ width 2.0))) (hi-schedule-tax rows midpoint)) (hi-schedule-tax rows ti))))

; Form N-11 line 23: the standard deduction for the filing status.
(def hi-standard-deduction ((y HawaiiYear) (status fed/FilingStatus)) Money :cite ((law "HRS" "235-2.4")) (cond ((is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_MARRIED_FILING_JOINTLY) (. y 'standard_deduction_joint)) ((is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE) (. y 'standard_deduction_joint)) ((is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD) (. y 'standard_deduction_head_of_household)) (else (. y 'standard_deduction_single))))

; Form N-11 line 6e: the exemptions claimed. The filer, unless someone else
; can claim them; the spouse on a joint return; one more for each of them 65
; or over; and each dependent.
(def hi-exemption-count ((hh ret/Household) (status fed/FilingStatus) (tax-year Int)) Int :cite ((law "HRS" "235-54")) (+ (if (. hh 'taxpayer.can_be_claimed_as_dependent) 0 1) (if (state-joint? status) 1 0) (if (. hh 'taxpayer.can_be_claimed_as_dependent) 0 (state-senior-count hh status tax-year)) (state-dependent-count hh tax-year)))

; Hawaii's estimated tax: HRS § 235-97 and HAR § 18-235-97, worked through on
; Form N-210. It is written on the shared machinery in
; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; hawaiitaxcalc/estimated.go, whose answers golden/testdata/estimated/HI.json.gz
; holds.
;
; HRS § 235-97 sets Hawaii's own rate, threshold, due dates and percentages,
; and § 235-97(f)(4) adopts subsections (d), (e)(2), (e)(3), (h), (i), (j),
; (k) and (l) of 26 U.S.C. § 6654 with the due dates moved to the 20th and the
; required annual payment set at 60% or 100%. The charge is two-thirds of one
; percent a month or part of a month, which Form N-210 multiplies as .00667.
; The figures follow the department's forms, Form N-210 and its instructions
; for 2025 and Tax Facts 2019-3 (revised February 2026), and the answer's
; divergences say where the statute or the rule reads otherwise. A year with
; no figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as HRS § 235-97 and Tax Facts 2019-3 print them.
(defstruct HawaiiEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (this_year_rate Int) (last_year_rate Int) (due_dates (Slice Date)))

(deffigures hi-estimated-2026 HawaiiEstimatedYear 2026 (from hi-dotax-tax-facts-2019-3-2026 (threshold #usd"500.00" :at question-4) (this_year_rate 6000 :at question-4) (last_year_rate 10000 :at question-4) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-20" #date"2026-06-20" #date"2026-09-20" #date"2027-01-20") :at question-8)))

; it.
(defstruct HawaiiEstimatedRules (figures HawaiiEstimatedYear) (holidays (Slice Date)) (file_and_pay_by Date) (stop Date) (monthly Int) (period_ends (Slice Date)) (annualised_shares (Slice Int)) (explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation))

; How Hawaii's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these rules
; carry.
(= hi-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Hawaii expects estimated payments if you expect $500 or more of Hawaii tax due. That is the tax left after withholding and credits. Each quarter's shortfall is charged 2/3 of 1% for each month it stays unpaid. Part of a month counts as a full month." (slice "Your target is 60% of this year's Hawaii tax or 100% of last year's, if smaller. Withholding and estimated payments that reach it keep you clear of the penalty. There is no 110% figure for higher incomes. Last year's figure needs a Hawaii return covering a full twelve months. Someone who filed no Hawaii return last year has only the 60% figure." "Each payment is a quarter, due April 20, June 20, September 20 and January 20. January 20 is in the next year. A date on a weekend or holiday shifts to the next business day. In 2026 the June date shifts to June 22 and the September date to September 21. Withholding counts as paid evenly over the four dates. That holds unless you show when it was withheld. Filing and paying in full by January 31 removes the January payment's penalty. The charge on earlier shortfalls then stops at January 20." "There is no penalty if this year's tax less withholding is under $500. Nor is there one if you had no Hawaii tax due last year. That year must be twelve months, all as a Hawaii resident. The department can waive the penalty for a casualty or disaster. The same goes if you retired after 62 or became disabled with reasonable cause." "The charge is two-thirds of one percent of the shortfall, 8% a year. It applies for each month or part of a month the shortfall stays unpaid. A month runs from the 21st to the 20th, so one day late costs a full month. Form N-210 multiplies by .00667 a month. The charge stops when the shortfall is paid, or on April 20 of the next year. That is when the return is due. With uneven income, Schedule A of Form N-210 can lower the early payments. It uses 15%, 30%, 45% and 60% of the tax on annualised income.") "Hawaii's test on this year's tax is 60%, not 90%. Last year's test is 100% at every income, with no 110% step. The threshold is $500, not $1,000, and payments fall on the 20th, not the 15th. The charge is 2/3 of 1% for each month or part of one, not a daily rate. One day late costs a full month." (slice "HRS §§ 235-97, 231-21" "HAR § 18-235-97" "Tax Facts 2019-3, Estimated Income Tax for Individuals (rev. February 2026)" "Form N-210, Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, Estates, and Trusts, and its instructions (Rev. 2025)" "26 U.S.C. § 6654(e), (h), as adopted by HRS § 235-97(f)(4)")))

; The 2026 rules. The 2026 Form N-210 is not published, so its arithmetic is
; the 2025 form's with the 2026 dates; its percentages, threshold and rate are
; fixed in HRS § 235-97, which no act has changed since 2003. The rate is
; fixed by statute, so the months in 2027 up to the April 20 stop are charged
; at it too. June 20, 2026 is a Saturday and September 20, 2026 a Sunday, so
; those instalments are due Monday, June 22 and Monday, September 21; no HRS
; § 8-1 holiday falls on a 2026 due date or the business day after one, so
; none is listed. A figure's source must be for its year, so these are
; written out rather than deffigures.
(= hi-estimated-rules-2026 HawaiiEstimatedRules (make-struct HawaiiEstimatedRules :figures hi-estimated-2026 :holidays ((inst empty-slice Date)) :file_and_pay_by #date"2027-01-31" :stop #date"2027-04-20" :monthly 6670 :period_ends (slice #date"2026-03-31" #date"2026-05-31" #date"2026-08-31" #date"2026-12-31") :annualised_shares (slice 1500 3000 4500 6000) :explanation hi-estimated-explanation))

; Iowa's estimated tax: Iowa Code § 422.16(12), which adopts the method of
; 26 U.S.C. § 6654 at Iowa's own interest rate under § 421.7, worked through
; on IA 2210, which follows federal Form 2210's pattern. It is written on the
; shared machinery in returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and
; reproduces the Go rules in iowataxcalc/estimated.go, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/IA.json.gz holds.
;
; The shape is federal: the lesser of 90% of this year's tax and 100% or 110%
; of last year's, four equal instalments, and interest by the day. The
; figures and dates are Iowa's: instalments at the end of April, June,
; September and January, a $1,000 threshold from 2026, a late-start table
; that gives fewer instalments, and a penalty that runs to April 30. The
; figures follow the 2026 IA 1040ES and the 2025 IA 2210, except that the
; 2025 form's $200 threshold predates the act that set $1,000 for 2026, so the
; act's figure is used; the answer's divergences say where form and law
; differ. A year with no figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.
; One tax year's figures, as the 2026 IA 1040ES and the Department of
; Revenue's announcement of the 2026 interest rate print them.
(defstruct IowaEstimatedYear (tax_year Int) (threshold Money) (due_dates (Slice Date)) (shares (Slice Int)) (rates (Slice EstRate)) (factors (Slice EstRate)))

; The 2026 figures. The rate from January 1, 2027 isn't published: the
; factors end on December 31, 2026, and the penalty says so.
(deffigures ia-estimated-2026 IowaEstimatedYear 2026 (from ia-idr-form-ia-1040es-2026 (threshold #usd"1000.00" :at worksheet) (due_dates (slice #date"2026-04-30" #date"2026-06-30" #date"2026-09-30" #date"2027-01-31") :at payment-schedule) (shares (slice 2500 2500 2500 2500) :at worksheet)) (from ia-idr-interest-rate-2026 (rates (slice (EstRate #date"2026-01-01" #date"2026-12-31" 100000 "2025 IA 2210, line 24b: 10% per annum, .00027397 per day (01/01/26 - 12/31/26); IDR press release, October 21, 2025")) :at rate-2026) (factors (slice (EstRate #date"2026-01-01" #date"2026-12-31" 27397 "2025 IA 2210, line 24b: 10% per annum, .00027397 per day (01/01/26 - 12/31/26); IDR press release, October 21, 2025")) :at rate-2026)))

; How Iowa's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these rules
; carry.
(= ia-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "Iowa expects estimated payments once you expect $1,000 or more of tax due. That is Iowa tax beyond your withholding for 2026, up from $200 before. The penalty is interest, by the day, on each installment's shortfall." (slice "You avoid the penalty if withholding and estimated payments reach a target. It is the smaller of 90% of this year's Iowa tax or 100% of last year's. The 100% becomes 110% if federal AGI plus Iowa net modifications tops $150,000. The limit is $75,000 if married filing separately. Last year must be a full twelve months. If you had no Iowa tax due for it, no penalty is due this year." "A quarter is due at the end of each of April, June, September and January. For 2026 that is April 30, June 30 and September 30, and February 1, 2027. January 31 is a Sunday. Withholding is spread evenly over those dates unless you show when it was taken. If you first expected to need payments after April 1, start at the next date. The year's amount is then split over fewer, larger installments." "The penalty is charged at Iowa's interest rate, 10% a year for 2026. It is charged for each day an installment stays short. It stops on April 30 of the next year, when the return is due. A payment goes to the oldest shortfall first. The department can waive the penalty for a casualty or disaster. It can also do so if you retired at 62 or later or became disabled. That needs reasonable cause.") "Iowa uses the federal method with its own figures and dates. Payments fall at the end of April, June, September and January. The 110% test adds Iowa's net modifications to federal AGI. A late starter pays in fewer installments. The rate is set yearly, not quarterly. The penalty runs to April 30, not April 15. Farmers and fishers use IA 2210F." (slice "Iowa Code §§ 422.16(12), 421.7, 421.9A; 2025 Iowa Acts ch. 148, §§ 59, 60" "Iowa Admin. Code r. 701—308.6" "2026 IA 1040ES, Iowa Individual Estimated Income Tax Instructions" "2025 IA 2210, Iowa Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, and its instructions" "Iowa Department of Revenue, IDR Announces 2026 Individual Income Tax and Interest Rates (October 21, 2025)")))

; The 2026 rules. No 2026 IA 2210 is published, so its figures are the 2025
; form's, with the 2026 dates: the $200 small-balance test, the 90%, 100%
; and 110% tests and their steps, the late-start table and the April 30
; stop. A figure's source must be for its year, so these are written out
; rather than deffigures. No Iowa holiday is listed: Iowa Code § 421.9A names
; its holidays by category, the first three 2026 due dates are weekdays, and
; January 31, 2027 is a Sunday, so the fourth moves to February 1.
(= ia-estimated-rules-2026 IowaEstimatedRules (make-struct IowaEstimatedRules :figures ia-estimated-2026 :form_threshold #usd"200.00" :this_year_rate 9000 :last_year_rate 10000 :high_income_rate 11000 :high_income_agi #usd"150000.00" :high_income_agi_separate #usd"75000.00" :late_groups (slice #date"2026-04-02" #date"2026-06-02" #date"2026-09-02") :stop #date"2027-04-30" :explanation ia-estimated-explanation))

(= ia-estimated-years (Table Int IowaEstimatedRules) (table 2026 ia-estimated-rules-2026))

; Form 40, Idaho Individual Income Tax Return, for full-year residents.
;
; The return starts from the prepared federal return: federal AGI, the
; federal filing status, the federal deductions, and the dependents the
; federal return claims.
;
; The rules cite Idaho Code Title 63, Chapter 30. The parts of the form and
; its instructions they implement name them in sources/catalog/id/2025.
; Whether the filer is someone else's dependent, line 12c.
(def id-claimable? ((hh ret/Household)) Bool :cite ((law "Idaho Code" "63-3022")) (any-of (. hh 'taxpayer.can_be_claimed_as_dependent)))

; Whether a status takes the joint standard deduction and filing requirement.
(def id-joint-figures? ((status fed/FilingStatus)) Bool :cite ((law "Idaho Code" "63-3022")) (or (state-joint? status) (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_QUALIFYING_SURVIVING_SPOUSE)))

; The addition to the standard deduction for each box checked on lines 12a
; and 12b: one amount if single or head of household, another if married.
(def id-additional-amount ((y IdahoYear) (status fed/FilingStatus)) Money :cite ((law "Idaho Code" "63-3022")) (if (or (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_SINGLE) (is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD)) (. y 'additional_unmarried) (. y 'additional_married)))

; The standard deduction for a filing status before any addition.
(def id-basic-standard-deduction ((y IdahoYear) (status fed/FilingStatus)) Money :cite ((law "Idaho Code" "63-3022")) (cond ((id-joint-figures? status) (. y 'standard_deduction_joint)) ((is status 'fed/FILING_STATUS_HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD) (. y 'standard_deduction_hoh)) (else (. y 'standard_deduction_single))))

(defworksheet id-standard-deduction ((y IdahoYear) (status fed/FilingStatus) (claimable Bool) (earned Money) (boxes Int)) Money :cite ((law "Idaho Code" "63-3022")) (line 1 "Standard deduction for your filing status" (id-basic-standard-deduction y status)) (line 3 "Earned income plus $450, or $1,350 if more" (max (. y 'dependent_minimum) (+ earned (. y 'dependent_addition)))) (line 4 "The smaller of lines 1 and 3 for a dependent, otherwise line 1" (if claimable (min line1 line3) line1)) (line 5 "Boxes checked on lines 12a and 12b times $1,600, or $2,000 if single or head of household" (* (id-additional-amount y status) (int-to-float boxes))) (line 6 "Standard deduction: add lines 4 and 5" (+ line4 line5)) (result line6))

; 5a; above it, line 5e less the property taxes on lines 5b and 5c.

; amount is taxed at 5.3%, in whole dollars.

; Illinois's estimated tax: Illinois Income Tax Act §§ 803, 804 and 806 (35
; ILCS 5/803, 5/804, 5/806), with the penalty rates of the Uniform Penalty
; and Interest Act § 3-3 (35 ILCS 735/3-3), worked through on Form IL-2210.

; returns/rules/federal/10_estimated_lib.tlisp and reproduces the Go rules in
; illinoistaxcalc/estimated.go, whose answers
; golden/testdata/estimated/IL.json.gz holds.
;
; The penalty is not interest. Each amount paid late is charged once, 2% if
; it is paid within 30 days of the due date and 10% if it is paid later or
; not at all. The rest is close to federal in shape: 90% of this year's tax

; Indiana's estimated tax: IC 6-3-4-4.1, with the penalty of IC

; for the annualized method. It is written on the shared machinery in

; holds.
;
; IC 6-3-4-4.1(a) has the payments made as 26 U.S.C. § 6654 provides, so the
; tests look federal: 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's, 110%
; above $150,000 of federal AGI, four quarters, nothing under $1,000. The
; charge does not. It is a flat 10% of each quarter's shortfall, so a payment
; one day late costs as much as one made months late, and making up a
; shortfall later does not reduce it. County income tax is collected with the
; state's and counts in every figure. The figures follow the department's
; forms, the 2026 Form ES-40 and the 2025 Schedules IT-2210 and IT-2210A, and
; the answer's divergences say where the Indiana Code reads otherwise. A year
; with no figures is answered ESTIMATED_OUTCOME_NO_RULES.

; How Kansas's estimated tax works, written by hand for the years these rules
; carry.
(= ks-estimated-explanation ret/EstimatedExplanation (est-explanation "You pay estimated tax once Kansas tax less withholding and credits reaches $500. The penalty is interest on what was short at each quarter. The rate is set for each calendar year." (slice "Your target is 90% of this year's Kansas tax or 100% of last year's, if smaller. Withholding and estimated payments should reach it a quarter at a time. If they do, you're clear of the penalty. There's no 110% tier for higher incomes. If you filed no Kansas return last year, or it showed no tax, no penalty arises. Kansas's penalty schedule counts last year's tax as zero in either case. The law is narrower. It gives zero only if no return was required, or last year's tax was under $200." "Four equal quarters are due April 15, June 15, September 15 and next January 15. A date on a weekend or legal holiday is due the next workday instead. Withholding counts as paid evenly across the four dates, whenever it was taken. Filing and paying in full by January 31 replaces the January payment." "The penalty is figured on Schedule K-210. At each date, interest is charged by the day on the total still short. It runs until the next date or until it's paid. After January 15, it runs until it's paid or April 15. Each year's rate is the prior July's federal underpayment rate plus one point. It is 8% for 2026. If your income came unevenly, the annualized method can lower early quarters.") "Unlike federal, the threshold is $500, not $1,000, and there's no 110% tier. No return or no tax last year means no penalty, with no federal full-year test. The rate is set once a year at the federal rate plus one point. Withholding can't be credited on the dates it was taken. Kansas has no casualty, retirement or disability waiver." (slice "K.S.A. 79-32,101, 79-32,102, 79-32,103, 79-32,107 and 79-2968" "Kansas Department of Revenue, K-40ES, Kansas 2026 Individual Estimated Tax (rev. 8-26-25)" "Kansas Department of Revenue, Schedule K-210, Kansas Underpayment of Estimated Tax, 2025, and its instructions (rev. 9-15-25)" "Kansas Department of Revenue, 2025 Kansas Individual Income Tax booklet, Form K-40 lines 18 to 31")))
